title: Autonomy policy
description: Which actions run on their own and which need a person (PROP-0008, design/approvals.md). Each action class maps to auto, notify, ask, or forbid. A project policy may only be stricter than the studio policy it narrows.

version.description: Changes whenever the policy's effect changes; decisions name it.

narrows.description: The studio policy a project policy narrows, by id.

default.description: The mode of an action class no rule names. Fail closed: never auto or notify.

commands.description: Command lines judged as `workspace-write` rather than as `command`: a command whose argv equals a listed line word for word (words split on single spaces), with no further arguments. Matching is exact, never by prefix; any other command is the `command` class, and a `command` mode of forbid applies to listed commands too. An entry with an empty word or a shell metacharacter is refused when the policy loads, and an argv word holding one is forbidden.

expiry.description: How long an approval request waits before it is denied (fail closed).

batch.description: How open requests are grouped for the operator: at most `maxSize` per batch, and a batch is presented once its oldest request has waited `maxWaitSeconds`.

riskTiers.description: 1.1 adds the path map that gives each path a change touches a risk tier (PROP-0016 §4, ADR-0071). A path's tier is the highest of the rules that match it, and a path no rule matches, or that cannot be read, is heavy; a change's tier is the highest of its paths'. With no applying policy carrying one, tiering is off.

version.description: The map's own version: it changes whenever a path's tier changes, and a tier decision names it.

tierByRisk.description: 1.2 adds the intelligence tier a board task's step takes at its task's risk tier (ADR-0073): under a risk tier, a step's capability (develop, review, validate) or kind of work (docs) mapped to the tier that becomes the step's minimum, such as heavy: { develop: frontier, review: frontier } and light: { validate: economy, docs: economy }. A step several entries match takes the highest of them; an escalated step is never lowered. Applied when the step is routed and its task has a risk tier, recorded as a decision that names the map's version. With no applying policy carrying one, steps keep their templates' tiers.

version.description: The map's own version: it changes whenever an entry changes, and a tier decision names it.

webAccess.description: 1.3 adds web access of a research role (ADR-0074): a WebSearch or WebFetch call of a Worker run under the named role profile runs unasked when the egress check passes on its query or URL and the run's content is classified at most maxClassification, at most maxWebCallsPerRun per run; past the bound, on an egress refusal, or for any other role, it asks. external-send still always asks in every rule: the agent gate applies a grant only to a call the policy said ask for. The studio policy must grant it; a project policy that carries webAccess only narrows it.

version.description: The grants' own version: it changes whenever a grant does, and each web call's decision names it.

profile.description: The role profile whose Workers' runs it is for: research, a read-only role whose only tools are reads and web calls.

maxWebCallsPerRun.description: The calls one run makes under it, 40 when unset; past it, a call asks.

maxClassification.description: A run whose content is classified above it sends nothing under it; local-private never does.

tierByStep.description: A step's capability or kind of work, mapped to the intelligence tier it takes at this risk tier.

paths.description: Repository-relative path patterns: segments split on /; * matches within one segment, ** any number of whole segments; a pattern ending in / is that directory and everything below it.

mode.description: auto: run, recorded; notify: run, recorded, and shown to the operator after; ask: an approval request, the action waits; forbid: denied.

requires.description: Deterministic checks that must pass before an auto or notify action counts as allowed; a failed check goes back to the lead, not to the operator.

expiresSeconds.description: For ask: this class's expiry, within expiry.maxSeconds.

allOf.description: Irreversible actions, the investor's own decisions, and a promotion always ask, even unattended.
